newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares finish down on lack of impetus.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares finish down on lack of impetus.

text.p: * Value of shares traded small at 2.6 billion pesos
Manila shares ended lower on Tuesday after being wedged in a tight range for most of the session on lack of significant news, traders said.
"The absence of market-lifting news put the focus on the very few stocks with stories," said Louie Bate, ING Baring sales head.
The main index closed 8.35 points down at 3,280.99.
Volume of shares traded were 15.86 billion valued at 2.761 billion pesos, well-below the 3.5 to 4.0 billion peso average volume in recent days.
Losers outnumbered gainers 65 to 46 with 88 issues unchanged. The oil, finance and mining sectors rose while the commercial-industrial, all shares and property sub-indices fell.
Victorias Milling Co, battered last week by its debt problems, strongly rebounded closing 60 centavos higher, or up 18.75 percent, to 3.80 pesos.
"We might see investors going back to the oil and mining issues considering the lack of interest on blue chips today," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital.
Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asia Merit Securities, said the market wil remain selective with focus still on secondliners with stories to tell.
